I have come close to death a few times in life, but none were as interesting as the time that I almost died in the Amazon.

As a kid, I had asthma. It only happened in cold weather or if I really exerted myself (like if I ran for several miles in the heat). I hadn't had an attack since I was about 12, so I assumed that I'd outgrown it, especially since I ran regularly and didn't have any problems.

Well, I was wrong!

And I found that out while on another 10km trek in the rainforest.

It was over 90 degrees F and we were returning from a trip to[ this lovely place](http://i.imgur.com/D4mA3ki.jpg).

The thing about the Amazon is that you must do a lot of climbing to get from point A to point B. We're talking regularly climbing 3-4 foot walls of earth or stone, along with fast paced hiking.

I was mostly unprepared for the climbing.

I made it to the water hole, but on the way back, we were given a choice: take a longer, more round-about way, or a shorter, harder hike back to camp.

The group decided to take the shorter hike. I agreed with it, thinking that I'd be ok, if tired. I almost made it without incident, too. It wasn't until the last half mile that I felt my lungs seize up. I couldn't get enough air in. From what I'm told, I made a gasping sound. My husband and best friend were terrified, but I acted on instinct. Stopping to rest would mean that I'd lose consciousness or fall and die, as the ledge we were on was a good 50 feet high.

With the strength I had, I instructed my group to keep moving. My husband and friend helped me climb the path for the last half mile, and I somehow made it back to camp, where I recovered over the course of half an hour or so.

I wasn't scared, but I did get a new inhaler when I returned home, if only to make my husband happy.

So there. I almost died in the Amazon. How many people can say they did that? ;)
